findings.title: Stripe webhook processes unsigned events
findings.description: The Stripe webhook parses the request body as JSON and passes it to process_verified_event without verifying the Stripe-Signature header, so anyone on the internet can submit forged billing events.
findings.root_cause: Commit c3d4e5f replaced stripe.Webhook.construct_event(payload, sig_header, settings.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) with await request.json() so that tests posting unsigned payloads would pass.
findings.exploit_path: An unauthenticated internet client POSTs a forged invoice.paid event for any invoice ID to /api/v1/webhooks/stripe; process_verified_event treats it as verified and enqueues the invoice as paid.
conditions: The webhook route is public by design (documented opt-out).

trace.description: event = await request.json() parses attacker-controlled JSON without signature verification.
The unverified event is enqueued as a trusted billing event.

evidence.description: Neither construct_event nor the Stripe-Signature header is used at the head SHA.
The test posts an unsigned payload and asserts 200, which drove the regression.

remediation.strategy: Restore signature verification over the raw body before any parsing and reject failures with 400; restore the rate limit that issue #471 requires.
remediation.regression_test: Post events with a missing and an invalid Stripe-Signature header and assert 400; sign test payloads with a test webhook secret instead of disabling verification.

likelihood.reason: The endpoint is public by design and needs no credentials.

impact.reason: Forged events can mark arbitrary invoices as paid and trigger provisioning.

confidence.reason: The branch history shows the control being removed, and no other verification layer exists at the head SHA.

findings.title: Invoice PDF rendering relies on route middleware only
findings.description: A reviewer suspected that the CLI export path reaches render_invoice_pdf without the route's permission check.
findings.claimed_root_cause: render_invoice_pdf was assumed to rely on route middleware for its role check.

trace.description: Service function shared by the HTTP route and the CLI export command.

evidence.description: require_permission(principal, "invoice:read") runs inside the service before rendering.

findings.reason: The role check lives inside the service function, so every entry point, including app/cli/export.py, is covered. Tenant scoping is a separate root cause tracked under AUTHZ-05.

findings.title: Invoice download trusts a client-supplied tenant_id
findings.description: download_invoice_pdf scopes the invoice lookup with a tenant_id query parameter instead of the authenticated principal, so any authenticated user can download another tenant's invoices.
findings.root_cause: The handler declares tenant_id: str as a query parameter and filters on Invoice.tenant_id == tenant_id; principal.tenant_id is never used, and the service's role check does not compare tenants.
findings.exploit_path: A user of tenant A calls GET /api/invoices/4812/pdf?tenant_id=<tenant B> and receives tenant B's invoice PDF.
conditions: The caller holds any valid session.

trace.description: Authenticated GET route accepts invoice_id and a tenant_id query parameter.
The ORM query filters on the client-supplied tenant_id.
The foreign invoice is rendered and streamed to the caller.

evidence.description: Invoice.tenant_id == tenant_id uses the query parameter.
require_permission(principal, "invoice:read") checks the role only; it never compares invoice.tenant_id with principal.tenant_id.

remediation.strategy: Derive the tenant from the verified principal, scope the lookup to it, and return 404 when the scoped lookup finds nothing.
remediation.regression_test: Request another tenant's invoice ID, with and without a tenant_id parameter, and assert 404.

likelihood.reason: Any authenticated user can change one query parameter.

impact.reason: Cross-tenant disclosure of invoice PDFs that contain customer billing data.

confidence.reason: The source trace is complete and no middleware, ORM default scope, or row-level security binds the tenant.

findings.title: External billing worker may act on invoice IDs without re-verifying the tenant
findings.description: The webhook path enqueues jobs that carry only an invoice ID taken from the event; the consumer lives in another repository, so whether it re-verifies tenant ownership cannot be established here.
findings.claimed_root_cause: enqueue_invoice_job sends invoice_id from the event payload with no trusted tenant envelope, and the consumer's scoping is not visible.

trace.description: Webhook events reach the billing event processor.
The job payload carries only invoice_id from the event.

evidence.description: enqueue_invoice_job(invoice_id=event["data"]["object"]["id"]) publishes to the billing-jobs queue without a tenant envelope.

blockers: The billing-jobs consumer (acme/billing-worker) is not part of this repository.

validation_plan.owner: Ask the billing-worker owners to confirm that the consumer reloads each invoice scoped to a tenant from a trusted envelope before acting, and to link that code.
validation_plan.local: After fixing API-07, add a test asserting that enqueued jobs carry the tenant resolved from the verified Stripe account mapping, not from free-form event metadata.
